title: On‑Prem Residency fallback quarantine and signed evidence export workflow
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers using Private (VPC / on‑prem) deployments require provable residency guarantees during regional outages. Current platform rollbacks and failover lanes lack a quarantine mode and a canonical signed evidence export that proves where data was processed and retained during any evacuation or fallback window.

Scope: Implement a 'residency quarantine' state for private control planes and agents, plus an automated, tamper-evident evidence export (signed manifests + certificate chain) for every failover event. This ticket covers control plane orchestration changes, agent-side hooks for evidence collection, KMS signing integration, and a first pass of UI/CLI export utilities and API endpoints used by compliance teams and auditors.

Out of scope: Full legal packaging for third‑party auditors, long‑term archival of exports (S3 lifecycle), and marketplace integrations. Those will be follow‑ups.
acceptance_criteria:
- Control plane exposes a new 'quarantine' target state that is used automatically when regional evacuation is initiated or customer policy gate prevents cross-region execution.
- Agents running in customer VPC/on‑prem transition to quarantine and stop processing non‑local requests within the configured 'evacuation grace window' (configurable per-customer).
- Evidence export endpoint /api/private/residency/export returns a ZIP with: signed-manifest.json, agent-kv-hash.txt, per-node telemetry snapshot, and a PEM-signed manifest identity chain.
- Signed manifests use customer KMS keys (via configured KMS/HSM integration) or fallback to Redwood attestation keys where customer keys are not provided; proof format documented.
- Tests: automated e2e that simulates region loss and validates manifest signatures, and unit tests for control plane state transitions.
- Documentation: Confluence runbook + UI page showing export workflow and how to verify signatures.
- No regression in normal (non-quarantine) failover latency beyond 10% for control plane actions.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag gated rollout to internal staging with synthetic on‑prem agents (week 1). 2) Canary to 3 small customers who opt in and sign data‑processing addendum (week 2). 3) Gradual enable by project for Private customers with all telemetry and export retention hooks (week 3). 4) Post‑canary audit and enable default for new Private installs.
Rollback plan: revert control plane gating flag and invalidate any partially produced exports via revocation list (maintained in control plane) and versioned manifest format.
telemetry_and_alerting:
- Events: private.quarantine.enter, private.quarantine.exit, residency.export.created, residency.export.failed, residency.signature.verified.
- Metrics: quarantine_active_customers, avg_export_generation_ms, export_sign_fail_rate.
- Alerts: export_sign_fail_rate > 1% for 15m (pager), private.quarantine.enter with customer impact high (pager).
- Dashboards: per-customer timeline view with state transitions and export artifacts linked.
notes_and_risks:
- Risk: Customers without KMS integration may require Redwood-hosted signing — document legal/contract implications.
- Risk: Large on‑prem fleets may produce very large evidence bundles; add streaming export and size caps.
- Risk: Signing latency could add 2–5s per-agent during export; mitigate with parallel signing and async bundle generation.
- Constraint: Evidence format must be verifiable offline; use RFC7515-like JSON structure and include canonicalization steps in docs.
- Stakeholders: PM (Marisol Vega), Security (Diego Ramos), Legal (Rina Singh), Support (Tomas Müller).
